articles.summary: Papa León XIV sigue su recuperación en El Vaticano y presidirá el miércoles la audiencia general
articles.body_text: León XIV, operado la pasada semana de un tumor canceroso en el pulmón, sigue su recuperación en el Palacio Apostólico vaticano y el próximo miércoles volverá a celebrar la habitual Audiencia General en la Plaza de San Pedro, informaron fuentes de la oficina de prensa de la Santa Sede. El pontífice permanecerá en El Vaticano, según las citadas fuentes, y no se desplazará esta semana a la localidad de Castelgandolfo -a unos 30 kilómetros de Roma- como solía hacer antes de su operación para descansar la tarde del lunes y el martes. El papa estadounidense-peruano, de 71 años, fue intervenido el pasado 13 de octubre en el hospital Gemelli de Roma por un adenocarcinoma (un tipo de cáncer) en una cirugía en la que le extirparon el lóbulo inferior del pulmón derecho. El sábado recibió el alta hospitalaria tras una favorable recuperación y regresó al Vaticano, donde el domingo volvió a presidir el rezo del ángelus.El propio León XIV explicó públicamente tras la plegaria que, una vez superada la “delicada” etapa de la operación, retomará gradualmente sus actividades. Además de la audiencia general del miércoles, para esta semana se prevé que León XIV reciba el jueves o viernes a los participantes del Congreso Internacional sobre la Pastoral Escolar y Universitaria que, con el lema “Trazando nuevos caminos de esperanza”, se celebrará los días 22 y 23 de octubre en el Aula Pablo VI del Vaticano.

articles.title: Lluvias en Piura inundan calles y dificultan el tránsito en varios sectores | FOTOS
articles.summary: Las lluvias registradas el 19 y 20 de octubre dejaron calles inundadas en Piura y dificultaron el tránsito en varios sectores de la región.
articles.body_text: Las intensas lluvias registradas el lunes 19 y el martes 20 de octubre dejaron calles anegadas en distintos sectores de Piura y complicaron el tránsito vehicular y peatonal. Las precipitaciones también se reportaron en localidades como Chulucanas y Tambogrande, en medio de las condiciones atmosféricas y oceánicas asociadas al fenómeno el niño. El Servicio Nacional de Meteorología e Hidrología del Perú (Senamhi) informó que las lluvias estuvieron relacionadas con un núcleo convectivo ubicado en la zona media alta de Piura. Asimismo, su radar identificó precipitaciones de ligera a moderada intensidad en diversas zonas de la costa. En distritos como Castilla, el agua acumulada en las calles generó preocupación entre los vecinos y dificultó el desplazamiento de vehículos y peatones. El Senamhi informó que las altas temperaturas diurnas y nocturnas continuarán en la costa peruana hasta el 31 de octubre, debido a las condiciones atmosféricas y oceánicas vinculadas al Niño Costero. Durante este periodo, se prevé cielo nublado en las primeras horas de la mañana, menor cobertura nubosa hacia el mediodía y la tarde, y un posterior incremento de la nubosidad. También se esperan lluvias dispersas en sectores de la costa norte. De acuerdo con el pronóstico, las temperaturas máximas en Piura y Tumbes oscilarán entre los 32 °C y 38 °C. A las condiciones meteorológicas se suma la persistencia de temperaturas superficiales del mar superiores a los valores habituales frente al litoral de Piura. Según información de la Dirección de Hidrografía y Navegación (DHN), al 18 de octubre la temperatura superficial del mar alcanzó los 26,2 °C en Talara y los 25,9 °C en Paita. Las anomalías registradas fueron de +8,1 °C y +8,5 °C, respectivamente. Estas condiciones favorecen temperaturas del aire por encima de lo normal, tanto durante el día como en la noche. Según el reporte, mientras persistan las anomalías positivas de la temperatura del mar, se prevé que el calor continúe durante las próximas semanas.

articles.title: Incendios forestales en Cusco: cifra de fallecidos se eleva a ocho
articles.summary: Los incendios forestales en Cusco dejaron ocho fallecidos, luego del hallazgo de un cuerpo calcinado en la provincia de Espinar, cuya identidad aún debe ser confirmada por las autoridades.
articles.body_text: La cifra de fallecidos por los incendios forestales en Cusco se elevó a ocho tras el hallazgo del cuerpo calcinado de un hombre de 34 años en la provincia de Espinar. La víctima sería un pastor que permanecía desaparecido desde el incendio que afectó la zona durante el último fin de semana, aunque las autoridades aún deben confirmar su identidad. Los restos fueron encontrados por comuneros en el sector de Chipta, perteneciente a la comunidad campesina de Ccahuaya, en Alto Pichigua, Espinar. El hombre, identificado como Frank Morales, era buscado por los pobladores desde que se reportó su desaparición tras el siniestro. Según la información disponible, los familiares habrían reconocido parcialmente el cuerpo. Sin embargo, corresponde a las autoridades determinar si los restos pertenecen efectivamente al hombre desaparecido. De acuerdo con el Centro de Operaciones de Emergencia Regional (COER) Cusco, hasta la fecha se han registrado 371 incendios forestales en la región, que afectaron aproximadamente 13.300 hectáreas. El reporte de la Oficina Regional de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres y Seguridad del Gobierno Regional de Cusco, difundido el miércoles 21 de octubre, confirmó que el número de fallecidos por estas emergencias ascendió a ocho. Asimismo, el informe indicó que, de los ocho incendios reportados hasta ese día en las provincias de Calca, Chumbivilcas, Anta, La Convención y Canchis, dos permanecían sin ser liquidados. La información proporcionada menciona a Anta en dos ocasiones al detallar las zonas afectadas. Según los reportes sobre el caso, el hombre hallado en Espinar trabajaba como pastor en la zona y tenía una condición médica especial que le habría dificultado escapar de las llamas. Tras el incendio, sus familiares perdieron sus pertenencias y solicitaron ayuda estatal para cubrir los gastos del sepelio y entierro.

articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

articles.title: Airbnb limits chores for guests, sparking backlash from hosts | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Hosts are threatening to leave the platform after Airbnb says that they can no longer require guests to strip beds or do other time-consuming cleaning chores.
articles.body_text: Airbnb is taking steps to limit the chores that hosts can require of guests prior to checkout, addressing a long-standing grievance among customers who often pay cleaning fees and are told they must do a list of tasks themselves. In a new policy update , Airbnb prohibits hosts from mandating that guests strip beds, wash and put away dishes, start laundry, or remove trash from the property. This new guideline will apply to reservations made on or after November 20. This change comes in response to years of backlash regarding overly burdensome checkout instructions and hefty fines for not disposing of trash. Many guests have voiced their frustrations on social media, questioning why they should be responsible for cleaning tasks after already paying a cleaning fee. However, some hosts aren’t pleased with the update. Within Airbnb’s community forums , some argue that basic cleaning responsibilities are essential for maintaining sanitary conditions and protecting their properties. They point out that hosts must manage the costs and practical demands of preparing their properties for the next guests. One host expressed concern that the new policy leans towards a hotel-like model, which detracts from the unique appeal of Airbnb. “Guests are given complete freedom to be lazy while the hosts bear the risk,” the host wrote. “The major distinction between commercial hotels and my private home is the personal touch. Guests can certainly be expected to wash their dishes or put them in the dishwasher and remove their dirty linens. In exchange, they enjoy a personal connection and a unique environment that a hotel simply can’t provide. Plus, every potential guest has the opportunity to read the listing beforehand and decide what they prefer. If these restrictions are removed, it could lead me to withdraw my listing and bid farewell to Airbnb after twelve years.” Airbnb has outlined some exceptions to the new policy, though. Hosts may still ask guests to conserve water during droughts or use bear-proof trash containers in areas where wildlife poses a risk. The policy change highlights the challenge Airbnb faces in balancing the expectations of guests versus hosts, and is another step taken in addressing guests’ concerns. The company faced scrutiny in 2024 over price transparency from hosts tacking on cleaning fees after guests booked their listings. In 2023, the company said more than 260,000 hosts had reduced or eliminated their cleaning fees. In May 2025, Airbnb began displaying total prices — including fees but excluding taxes — by default in search results worldwide. It will be interesting to see how many hosts decide the new restrictions make Airbnb less attractive as a platform. But the move could also draw in more travelers who want the convenience of a rental without feeling as though they are both paying for housecleaning while still expected to clean the home themselves. articles.title: Meta says Muse has over 10M users, with shopping a top activity | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Meta Muse users are adopting the app for shopping and personal productivity, the company said during Q3 earnings. The AI app now has over 10M users.
articles.body_text: Meta said during its third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday that its AI app Muse has been adopted by more than 10 million users, confirming estimates released earlier this week by market intelligence firm Sensor Tower. But it is how people are using it, and how much they’re spending that has caught CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s attention. Zuckerberg said about 25% of people who set up Muse now use it daily, helping improve retention. He also shared that over a quarter of Muse’s engaged users who were shopping via the AI agent, had an average purchase size of over $200, which was surprising even to industry insiders. “Plaid told us that they hadn’t seen activity like they’re seeing with their connector on any other service before,” Zuckerberg said, referring to the financial technology company that connects payment apps to customers’ bank accounts. Muse uses Plaid’s connector to enable agentic shopping. Now that Muse has achieved “product-market fit,” Zuckerberg said Meta’s focus will shift to scaling the AI agent, increasing revenue, and optimizing its compute costs. Remarkably, the tech company is forecasting that Muse will eventually bring in more revenue per user than its “family of apps” users do today — meaning its users on Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger. Currently, that figure is around “several hundreds of dollars annually,” Zuckerberg said. Meta has said it ultimately intends to monetize Muse by keeping it free for most users, but keeping a percentage of the commerce taking place on the platform. Power users who want access to the most advanced AI models or more tokens will also have to pay. Zuckerberg also noted that Meta believes Muse will be profitable after it scales. “On the compute side, we are building out the capacity to serve more than a billion people over the next few years,” he told bankers and analysts on the Q3 earnings call. “In the near term, Muse is very compute-intensive to run, but we expect to improve its cost efficiency by more than 10x in the next year, which will enable it to be profitable once the revenue lines are at scale.” Muse will also play a central role in Meta’s smart glasses strategy. Reality Labs, the division responsible for smart glasses, VR, and the metaverse, is still losing billions. However, the division’s losses are expected to improve from $19.1 billion in 2025 to $15 billion this year. Beyond scaling and supporting its hardware strategy, Zuckerberg teased the company’s plans for something he called the “Muse network.” He described this as taking Muse from a “single-player game” to one where “your Muses can work with your friends’ and your families’ [Muses].” “And if you want to buy something, it’s not just navigating to that business’s website; it’s talking to their agent,” he added. articles.title: Year-old AI lab Flapping Airplanes raises $1B at a $6B valuation | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Just 9 months after raising an $180 million seed round, Flapping Airplanes has landed $1 billion Series A for its mission to build AI models "without ingesting half the internet."
articles.body_text: Year-old startup Flapping Airplanes has wowed Silicon Valley with an impressive founding team and a mission to find ways to train large models with less data. On Wednesday, the company announced it had raised a $1 billion Series A round, co-led by Index and Lux, reportedly at a $6 billion valuation. The round comes just nine months after the company launched with a $180 million seed round from GV, Sequoia, and Index. That seed round had valued the company at $1.5 billion, so its valuation just quadrupled. Other participants in the new round included earlier backers Sequoia, GV and Kleiner Perkins. Valor, Atreides, Kleiner Perkins, A*, and Nvidia are also investors in the company. Flapping Airplanes was founded by Aidan Smith and brothers Asher and Ben Spector. Smith is a former founder and Thiel fellow who worked at the brain implant company Neuralink during college. Asher Spector was a statistics PhD at Stanford, while Ben Spector was a computer science PhD student at Stanford and founded Prod while at MIT. Prod is an almost secret-society, five-year-old student-run startup accelerator that has “become one of the most powerful talent incubators in Silicon Valley,” wrote Sequoia partner David Cahn , a Flapping Planes investor, in a post earlier this year explaining why he invested. Together, the founders “are building the ‘young person’s AGI lab,’” as Cahn described it. The founders describe their work as “the world’s most complete megakernel framework. It can perform entire training runs, serve inference, play video games, and even do all three simultaneously in a single kernel.” (A kernel is a program that runs on a GPU, and a megakernel bundles many tasks into one program.) The founders claim the framework “can overlap memory-bound inference with compute-bound training,” meaning it can run a task that spends most of its time waiting for data to be fetched alongside one that spends most of its time doing math, so the chip is rarely sitting idle. The premise is that AI has barely scratched the surface of what GPUs can do, and they believe it can create intelligent systems “without ingesting half the internet.” The goal is systems that cost less to train and run. “A model that’s a million times more data efficient is probably a million times easier to put into the economy,” Asher Spector told TechCrunch shortly after the startup launched. They now have a fresh $1 billion to hire and attempt to turn that goal into reality. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Tesla starts Optimus robot production in California as profit falls 43% | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Tesla's revenue was flat and its expenses skyrocketed as it pressed the accelerator on its Optimus robots, AI, and autonomous driving.
articles.body_text: Tesla has started production of its Optimus humanoid robot at its factory in Fremont, California, in a manufacturing space once dedicated to making electric vehicles, the company announced Wednesday. “The bots coming off this line are the first production-quality bots that we have manufactured,” Tesla wrote in its third-quarter letter to shareholders. “While we will continue to iterate on the hardware and manufacturing process, we have proven that the current manufacturing process for Optimus is suitable for a commercial product.” Tesla CEO Elon Musk said on a conference call that he considers this “early production,” and that the ramp will be an slow and “somewhat bumpy because it is such a radically new product.” He nonetheless claimed Tesla will be able to make 20,000 of them per week by the end of 2027. “There’s still some things we need to tweak about the design, because you need to deliver a robot that is that is safe and reliable and has long duration, so it can’t like, wear out after a month,” he said. “And there’s still quite a lot of work to do with regard to the AI and the robot for it to be truly useful for open-ended tasks.” That fordward-looking development wasn’t enough to lift the company’s otherwise middling third-quarter earnings, results that typify a company at the midpoint of a major bet. Tesla’s revenue was flat and its expenses skyrocketed as it pressed the accelerator on its Optimus robots, AI, and autonomous driving. The end result was a 43% drop in profits. The company’s revenue was largely driven by EV sales, which were flat year-over-year at $20 billion. Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, about 6,000 more than the previous quarter, but fewer than in the same period last year. Tesla’s total third-quarter revenue was $28.04 billion, a skosh below the $28.09 billion it generated in the third quarter of 2025. Tesla’s third-quarter revenue was also about $200 million lower than the previous quarter’s haul of $28.23 billion. Tesla saw a 16% year-over-year drop in its solar and energy storage business to $2.8 billion, which it blamed on tariff-related customer refunds. There was some positive revenue growth in its services business, a category that includes customer subscriptions to its Full Self-Driving advanced driver-assistance software. Tesla’s services business grew 33% year-over-year, bringing in $4.6 billion. None of this was enough to outpace Tesla’s spending on artificial intelligence projects and its Optimus robot, which took a big bite out of profits. The company reported $787 million in net income, a 43% drop from the same period in 2025 when it earned $1.37 billion. Lower regulatory credit sales also put pressure on its profitability. The company stayed in the black in large part because of a big boost from its “services and other” segment, which accounted for a record $734 million in gross profit for the quarter. articles.title: Recursive launches Flint, a laptop coding model it says was largely built by AI | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Startup Recursive has released Flint, a free, laptop-sized coding model built largely by its own AI research system, as an early test of AI that improves itself.
articles.body_text: Recursive , an AI startup founded last year, is starting to live up to its name. The company, which is trying to build AI that can improve itself, released its first model, Flint , on Wednesday. Flint is a free coding model that can run on a laptop and was built largely with the help of AI. Recursive’s automated research system, which it calls the Eureka Machine, helped with nearly every step of Flint’s development, the company says. That let a small team build the model from scratch in under four months. Flint is an early public test of recursive self-improvement: the idea that AI can build better AI, which in turn builds even better AI. It’s also one of the most debated ideas in the industry. Some researchers fear that AI improving itself could slip out of human control. For now, Recursive’s version is more limited: an AI research assistant overseen by people that produced a model small enough for a laptop. The company emerged from stealth in May with $650 million in funding at a $4.65 billion valuation, from backers including GV, Nvidia, and AMD Ventures. Recursive is led by CEO Richard Socher, Salesforce’s former chief scientist. Because Flint runs on a user’s own computer rather than a company’s cloud servers, developers can use it offline, keep their code private, and avoid the usage fees that AI cloud services charge based on how much text the model processes. The model is free to download on Hugging Face, the popular site for sharing AI models, under the Apache 2.0 license, an open-source license that allows free use and modification. Flint is a mixture-of-experts model, meaning it uses only a small slice of itself for any given task: just 2.5 billion of its 40 billion settings, known as parameters, at a time. That makes it light enough for an ordinary laptop and far smaller than Meta’s Muse Spark Open , an open model built for Macs that was released last week. Muse Spark Open uses 816 billion parameters and needs at least a terabyte of memory. Flint is also fast. In Recursive’s tests, it generated about 131 tokens (chunks of text) per second on a MacBook Pro with Apple’s M4 Pro chip — roughly twice the 58 to 69 tokens per second that similar models managed on the same machine, including Google’s Gemma 4 and Nvidia’s Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. On Nvidia’s RTX Spark, Flint topped 150 tokens per second. On SWE-Bench Verified, a benchmark that measures how well AI can fix real-world software bugs, Flint outperformed other models under 50 billion parameters. On Recursive’s own average across six tests, only one model, Alibaba’s Qwen3.8 27B, scored higher than Flint. The company acknowledged that Flint would need more guidance than the big paid coding assistants, and suggested breaking large tasks into smaller steps. Still, early reviews were positive. Wired’s Will Knight used Flint on a Mac with 48GB of memory to build several small programs, including a to-do list app and a tool that scours the web for research. He found that smaller coding models often ran into errors or were slow compared to Claude or Codex, but Flint nailed his coding requests every time. The Eureka Machine comes up with ideas, runs experiments and uses the results to decide what to try next. According to the company’s launch video , it contributed to nearly every part of building Flint, from pre-training to post-training and inference. Recursive said that Eureka’s contributions include a sparser model shape, low-bit training that shrank Flint by 71% with almost no loss in quality and custom kernels, which are specialized programs that speed up the underlying computations. Recursive didn’t say how much time the Eureka Machine saved its researchers, but it’s not alone in leaning on AI to do research. OpenAI said last month that by mid-August, its AI agents were logging 3.1 workdays for every one worked by a human researcher.

articles.title: Automattic begins layoffs following board upheaval and executive departures | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Automattic has begun laying off employees across multiple teams, including WordPress.com and its enterprise business, following a board shakeup and a series of executive departures. Sources say more cuts could follow as the company looks to improve its finances.
articles.body_text: Automattic, the parent company to WordPress.com , WooCommerce, Tumblr, and others, has begun layoffs, and insiders tell us they are bracing for more cuts to come. Over at least the past week, the cuts have impacted its communications team, social team, WordPress.com , and its VIP enterprise business. The departures represent more turmoil at Automattic, whose team is still reeling from the board’s failed attempt to oust CEO Matt Mullenweg in September, resulting in a complete board turnover and other exec departures, including its CFO, interim CFO , and Chief Legal Officer. Automattic’s Director of Communications, Megan Fox, posted about her departure last week on LinkedIn, saying the move was an “unexpected end” and that her role had been “eliminated.” Meanwhile, after TechCrunch reported that Automattic’s interim Chief Financial Officer Jeremy Klaperman left earlier this month , only weeks after the board shakeup, Mullenweg posted on X suggesting Klaperman may have been “offended” by the company’s decision to seek external candidates to fill the role. (Internally, however, Mullenweg had asked Klaperman to reconsider leaving, we had heard.) At one point, Mullenweg also shared personal information about one of the recently departed execs in the company’s internal Slack, according to screenshots viewed by TechCrunch. The post related to a health matter impacting the person’s spouse, and claimed that the company was not providing this person with much-needed COBRA insurance. Mullenweg said the exec was threatening to sue over this. Mullenweg also shared that his own fiancée had been impacted by the same health condition. Some employees told us they were shocked that the CEO would share something so private and personal in such a forum. Throughout this month, TechCrunch has heard from different sources that members of Automattic’s team have also been let go, including those in marketing and product at WordPress.com. Reached for comment about the layoffs last week, Mullenweg said the terminations were not above its normal numbers. Asked on Wednesday about the growing total, Mullenweg said that today he was “mostly focused on PHP.” (He posted on X about the PHP security issue hitting the internet, which is taking priority.) The company’s About page lists the total number of staff at 1,397, but insiders tell us that the plan is likely to spread out the layoffs over the months ahead, in the hopes of improving Automattic’s Q4 revenue figures ahead of a debt renegotiation that’s coming up in June. articles.title: GM is betting compute and AI will help it compete with Chinese automakers | TechCrunch
articles.summary: To compete with Tesla, Rivian, and a host of Chinese automakers, GM’s fourth-gen EV platform will roll out a new central computer and electrical architecture that will debut in 2028 in the Cadillac Escalade IQ.
articles.body_text: When GM announced its new fourth-generation EV platform on Wednesday, what the automaker didn’t share was almost as notable as what it did. The new EV platform, part of a series of technology-focused announced during its annual GM Forward event in New York, didn’t talk about suspension geometries, dash-to-axle ratios, and torsional rigidity, all nerdy automotive terms that translate to how people will experience a car. Is it supple or sporty? Does it have a refined stance? When it hits a pothole, does it feel like a bank vault or a paper plate? Instead, GM’s announcement centered on novel battery chemistries, revamped electric motors, and an entirely new central computing platform and electrical architecture that will connect every system in the car, including acceleration and power, steering, braking, and active safety features as well as software. Lots and lots of software. “We think vehicles can become a more capable and helpful part of everyday life if we make them spaces that understand context, reduce friction, and give people back moments that would otherwise be consumed by the demands of the road,” Sterling Anderson, executive vice president, global product, and chief product officer at GM, told TechCrunch in a recent interview. That sure doesn’t sound like a traditional automaker’s pitch. Then again, since the arrival of Tesla, Rivian, and Chinese automakers, the industry hasn’t been the same. Ride and handling still matter, but they’re table stakes. What sets vehicles apart today is largely defined by software. Anderson has talked about this future GM before. Last year, the company announced plans to overhaul the electrical and computational guts of its future vehicles in a bid to deliver faster software, more capable automated driving features, and a custom, conversational AI assistant. This year, GM is providing more details and dates. This technological overhaul is set to debut in 2028 with the Cadillac Escalade IQ. The company will also rollout an autonomous highway driving feature in 2028 that will allow drivers to have their hands and eyes off the road and without the need to be ready to take over. European and U.S. automakers have spent years chasing the prospect of software-defined vehicles, but have often fallen short. Volkswagen Group had so much trouble with its own in-house effort, including its troubled Cariad unit, that it struck a $5.8 billion joint venture deal with relative newcomer Rivian. GM has been on its own capitally intensive software adventure. The company has bet heavily on software in recent years. It ditched the popular smartphone projection technology Apple CarPlay for nearly all of its EVs, and instead turned to a Google-based infotainment system, which is actually quite capable even if it doesn’t yet live up to the standards set by Tesla and Rivian. It’s poured billions into software and autonomous vehicle technology development too. GM’s capitalized software amortization expense in 2025 was $866 million, which gives a sense of how much it is spending even as it spreads out the cost over years. Like many legacy automakers, GM has come to the conclusion that the old approach to electronics, which scattered computer chips throughout the vehicle, was holding it back. For fourth-generation EVs, GM will centralize much of those functions on a Central Compute Unit (CCU) that’s 40-times more powerful than its existing systems. Eliminating smaller chips on the edges will help trim wiring by 30%, saving weight and simplifying assembly.

articles.title: While Amazon blocks AI agents, Walmart rolls out the welcome mat | TechCrunch
articles.summary: As Amazon blocks AI agents from shopping on its site, Walmart is taking the opposite approach, introducing new technology that lets AI agents make purchases on customers' behalf, with controls over spending and transaction approvals.
articles.body_text: Walmart is embracing agentic commerce with the launch of its own Agent Gateway to manage transactions and other new features aimed at customers using AI agents, the retailer announced on Wednesday. The move comes shortly after Walmart’s top competitor, Amazon, began blocking AI agents from making purchases on behalf of online shoppers. The company’s embrace of AI technology differentiates it from other online businesses, including not only Amazon but also various travel and booking sites, which have responded to the growing consumer adoption of AI agents by locking them out of their websites completely . Walmart, on the other hand, had already announced a partnership with a leading agent in the space, Meta’s Muse, and offers integrations with popular AI apps like ChatGPT, Gemini, and others. Now, it’s expanding on those efforts with more technology to prepare for a world where AI agents become mainstream, said Walmart President and CEO John Furner, speaking at the Masters of Scale Summit in San Francisco on Wednesday. The technology will support agentic shopping from both Walmart and the company’s discount warehouse, Sam’s Club. It starts with Walmart’s Agent Gateway, the company’s new MCP server, which is designed to help approved agents connect to Walmart over the model context protocol (MCP). The protocol, originally created by Anthropic, allows AI agents to connect to external data sources, tools, and other workflows. In this case, it lets an AI agent search across Walmart’s online inventory and make purchases on behalf of the agent’s user. What’s more, the retailer says that its Agent Gateway will be able to help customers shop for their usual brands or items without having to share their personal information or purchase history directly with the agent. The company has also developed new technology to differentiate an agent’s purchases from those initiated directly by the customer, and to give shoppers more control over what their agents can and cannot do. With Agent Profiles, rolling out next month, customers will be able to authorize each AI agent they use with a dedicated profile in their account, allowing them to see the agent’s purchases separately from their own. Plus, customers will be in control of how purchases get approved by either requiring approval for each transaction or by authorizing transactions within a certain spending limit they set. The retailer says these controls are similar to adding someone as an authorized user on your credit card, where their transactions are identified, and you can cap their spending. The Agent Profiles will be created the first time you use a given agent to shop through the Walmart Agent Gateway, the company notes. To get started, you’ll authorize and link the Agent Profile to your Walmart account, then set your controls or spending limits. You can also delete an Agent Profile at any time. Agent support is available for anyone with a Walmart account; a Walmart+ membership is not necessary. Alongside these technologies, Walmart is introducing special “terms” for AI agents, which specify how they must operate and what rights they have to transact on its site. Of note, Walmart says that its returns process applies, including when an agent doesn’t act as intended. That’s a customer-friendly condition that could sway consumers who were worried about being an early tester of agentic commerce, as they won’t fear ending up with products they don’t want because of a misbehaving agent. Walmart also says that agents can’t take actions beyond what the shopper intends, can’t access the customers’ payment information, and can only access the information they need for the given task. Agents that don’t comply with the terms will be blocked from accessing Walmart’s site. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: The internet is having a very bad cybersecurity day | TechCrunch
articles.summary: From AI-discovered PHP vulnerabilities to flaws in Node.js and popular AI tool LiteLLM, cybersecurity teams have plenty to worry about this week.
articles.body_text: The internet is having a bad day, from a cybersecurity perspective. Government websites around the world went offline , Reuters reported, after AI discovered critical security vulnerabilities that impacted the programming language PHP . The issues were severe enough that the U.S. National Security Agency (NSA) advised organizations using PHP on their systems to either immediately update or take their systems offline until they could. But the PHP update wasn’t the only headache cybersecurity folks were facing on Wednesday. Node.js , the open-source JavaScript runtime environment, also dropped a security surprise of its own when it shared that four high-severity vulnerabilities were just patched in its latest release. One allowed remote code execution, and two others would have permitted a TLS validation bypass, potentially allowing attackers to bypass checks intended to verify a server’s identity. In addition, LiteLLM, a popular open source proxy for routing requests to multiple LLM providers, was compromised by an attacker who injected malicious code, the company shared in a post on X on Wednesday afternoon. The malicious artifacts were published to PyPI (Python Package Index), Docker Hub , and GHCR (GitHub Container Registry), the post noted. The malicious code was said to include an information stealer that targeted cloud credentials, passwords, and AI service credentials, in addition to a remote access trojan that could allow hackers to execute commands on compromised systems. LiteLLM said it has now removed the malicious releases and images and advised anyone who installed them to follow the remediation guidance it provided. And wait, there’s more! An Indian certificate authority, eMudhra, had its private keys compromised , potentially allowing attackers to issue fraudulent certificates and impersonate legitimate websites. Security pros have called this a massive cleanup job and one that’s “bigger than Heartbleed .” (The latter is a reference to the critical security vulnerability in the OpenSSL cryptographic software library). These issues come on the heels of other security breaches and hacks, including the breach of the cloud-native database-as-a-service, TiDB Cloud, which the company announced on Monday. Other hackers have been exploiting four patched Plex Media Server flaws, collectively called Plex2Shell. And last week, cybersecurity company BeyondTrust warned customers to patch a critical zero-day in its Remote Support product, which had been exploited since August. Though the issues were unrelated to each other, their back-to-back arrival highlights the challenges cybersecurity teams now face. This is particularly important as AI could make it easier for attackers to exploit vulnerabilities once discovered. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . How Big Tech is swallowing the AI industry
articles.summary: Amazon has replicated an antitrust-avoidance playbook pioneered by Microsoft with its hiring of most of the team behind buzzy AI startup Adept.
articles.body_text: A couple of months ago, I was sitting in the audience at a tech conference in San Fransisco watching Bloomberg’s Emily Chang interview Reid Hoffman. She asked about Microsoft’s hiring of the team behind Inflection, a would-be OpenAI competitor that Hoffman co-founded. It was an acquisition in everything but name, clearly designed to avoid the scrutiny of antitrust regulators. Not only had Microsoft (where Hoffman is a board member) hired most of Inflection’s employees — it also licensed the startup’s technology in a way that seemed designed to make its investors whole. Speaking with Chang that day onstage, Hoffman predicted that what happened to Inflection will become a “pattern” for future AI deals. We are seeing that pattern play out now. Last Friday, Amazon announced that it is hiring most of the team behind Adept, another would-be OpenAI competitor that raised about $400 million from top-tier investors to build, in the words of CEO David Luan, “a new type of giant model that turns natural language into actions on your machine.” Alexandra Miller, an Amazon spokesperson, told The Verge that the company had hired “close to” to 66 percent of Adept’s employees. In an internal memo published by GeekWire’s Taylor Soper, SVP Rohit Prasad said that, like Microsoft with Inflection, Amazon will also be licensing Adept’s technology to “accelerate our roadmap for building digital agents that can automate software workflows.” Adept’s corporate blog post about the news suggests it was running out of money: “Continuing with Adept’s initial plan of building both useful general intelligence and an enterprise agent product would’ve required spending significant attention on fundraising for our foundation models, rather than bringing to life our agent vision.” Recent reports say the company has been looking to sell itself. The reality is that building leading AI models is extremely costly, and raising $400 million isn’t even enough to compete these days. Big Tech, meanwhile, is flush with cash and looking to get in on what everyone perceives to be the next big thing. It’s logical for more AI startups to go the way of Inflection and Adept as the industry consolidates. The problem for Big Tech is that they are no longer allowed to buy companies like they once did. The current antitrust enforcement regime would most certainly try to block an Amazon acquisition of Adept, whether there is a strong legal argument for doing so or not. (Amazon execs are still seething about not being allowed to buy a robot vacuum cleaner company.) Even still, capitalism finds a way. What Microsoft did to Inflection, and what Amazon just did to Adept, is the new Big Tech playbook for swallowing the AI industry and getting away with it. Silicon Valley has a storied history of acquihires, where a startup is gutted for its people and left for dead. Microsoft and Amazon have done what are essentially reverse acquihires, where the hiring of people and a corresponding licensing deal is designed to disguise what is actually an acquisition. Reid Hoffman, meanwhile, should probably be congratulated for more than just an accurate prediction about the future of these deals — one of Adept’s earliest investors was none other than his venture capital firm, Greylock. articles.title: Carl Bildt: Betydande risk för extraval
articles.summary: Regeringsförhandlingarna står still. Tidigare statsminister Carl Bildt (M) ser en ”betydande risk” för extraval.
articles.body_text: Tidigare statsminister Carl Bildt (M) ser en ”betydande risk” för extraval. – Det verkar som att skyttegravarna grävts ännu djupare, säger han i SVT:s Aktuellt. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. I förra veckan röstade riksdagen nej till Magdalena Andersson (S) som statsminister och sonderingsuppdraget gick vidare. Det ligger nu i händerna hos C-ledaren Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist. Hon hade tidigare bjudit in alla rödgröna partier till ett seminarium, men då diskuterade de inte regeringsfrågan. Hon hoppas nu på ett samarbete i ”den breda mitten” med KD, L, S och MP. Hon höll möte med Andersson om saken i går . Men S-ledaren ville inte kommentera om de gjort framsteg i regeringsbildningsprocessen. Den tidigare statsministern och utrikesminister Carl Bildt (M) tycker inte att det verkar som det. I SVT:s Aktuellt säger han att det finns en ”betydande risk” för ett extraval. – Det var tydligt under valrörelsen att vi var på väg mot ett resultat som skulle kunna leda till något sånt här, säger han. Bildt anser att det skulle krävas stora insatser från partiledarna för att de ska kunna få ihop en regering. I egna ord säger han att någon kommer behöva göra en ”saltomortal eller nästan pyramidal” för att få ihop det. Att partierna håller fast i sina röda linjer som låser läget är i sig inget märkligt, säger han. – Partier går till val på vissa saker och det är hederligt, men sen kan det visa sig oförenligt och att de inte lyckas lösa ut det. Då är extraval det instrument som finns för att lösa ut detta. En lösning på situationen ser han inte i nuläget.

Omkring 70 procent av världens sajter bygger på php, enligt statistisk från marknadsundersökningsföretaget W3Techs . Omkring 330 000 aktiva hemsidor i Sverige bygger på php, enligt analysverktyget Builtwith . – Det är så vanligt att det finns hundratals miljoner hemsidor i världen som bygger på det, säger John Ahlmark, kommunikatör vid FRA . – Exakt, eller ens ungefär, vad vi använder för programvaror tänker jag inte gå in på, säger John Ahlmark som uppger att ”oräkneliga verksamheter” bygger sina hemsidor på php. – De kan installera skadlig programkod som ransomware och stjäla, eller ändra datan på hela servern och göra så att det inte blir tillgängligt för användarna, säger Alexandre Bartel, professor och forskare inom programvaruteknik och datasäkerhet på Umeå universitet. articles.title: Moderat ”kupp” ger miljonstöd till SD i Stockholm
articles.summary: M, KD, C och L i Stockholms stad var överens om hur de skulle fördela resurserna som opposition. Trodde de.
articles.body_text: M, KD, C och L i Stockholms stad var överens om hur de skulle fördela resurserna som opposition. Trodde de. När avtalet skulle undertecknas visade det sig att M fört hemliga förhandlingar med SD – som nu får ett extra stöd värt flera miljoner kronor. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. I Stockholms stadshus dog inte alliansen. Moderaterna, Kristdemokraterna, Centerpartiet och Liberalerna håller fortfarande ihop, medan Sverigedemokraterna står utanför samarbetet. SD i Stockholm har genom åren präglats av både interna konflikter och avhopp. Inför valet lyftes röster om att släppa in SD men då sa Centerpartiet nej. Efter att de rödgröna vann valet och bildade ett nytt styre har de fyra partierna gått ihop för att fördela resurser och maximera det gemensamma inflytandet i opposition. Tjugo minuter innan kommunfullmäktiges sammanträde var det sagt att partierna skulle signera en överenskommelse för mandatperioden 2026-2030. Där regleras hur mycket pengar man får till sina respektive partikassor och kanslier. Alliansen hade förhandlat i flera veckor och till slut landat i ett kostnadsförslag. Men när det var dags att skriva under upptäcker de andra partierna att Moderaterna även haft en hemlig sidoförhandling med Sverigedemokraterna. Det presenterades av M-toppen Christofer Fjellner utan förvarning, beskriver källor.

Felaktigheter kan förekomma. ■ S tappar kraftigt i Norrland och backar i kommunvalet i 45 av 54 kommuner. ■ I Överkalix var raset störst, med 25,7 procentenheter. Även i regionvalet och riksdagsvalet tappar S i norra Sverige – där partiet traditionellt sett har haft ett starkt fäste. ■ Statsvetaren tror att S grepp om norr kan fortsätta att försvagas flera val framåt. I årets kommunval backar Socialdemokraterna i 45 av de 54 norrländska kommunerna. Det rör sig om allt från tapp på en knapp procentenhet – till katastrofval med ras på som mest 25,7 procentenheter i Överkalix. Och i riksdagsvalet tappar S i alla Norrlandskommuner. Därmed är trenden ett faktum: partiets dominans i norr glider dem ur händerna. – I hela Norrland har de haft ett betydande grepp om makten. Det är klart att det finns undantag i någon kommun här och där, men i Västernorrland, Västerbotten och Norrbotten har man varit otroligt starka, säger Simon Matti, professor i statsvetenskap vid Luleå tekniska universitet.

articles.title: Razzia mot högernationalister i EU – misstänks ha förskingrat miljoner
articles.summary: Polis och EU-åklagare har gjort en razzia på flera kontor i Europaparlamentet, rapporterar den europeiska nyhetssajten Rapporteur. Tillslaget sker efter att anställda hos högernationalistiska Patriots misstänks ha förskingrat flera miljoner euro i bidrag.
articles.body_text: Polis och EU-åklagare har gjort en razzia på flera kontor i Europaparlamentet, rapporterar den europeiska nyhetssajten Rapporteur . Tillslaget sker efter att anställda hos högernationalistiska Patriots misstänks ha förskingrat flera miljoner euro i bidrag. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Polis och åklagare gjorde på onsdagsförmiddagen en razzia mot kontor tillhörande anställda på den högernationalistiska partigruppen Patriots for Europe i EU-parlamentet , skriver flera europeiska medier. Åklagarna kommer från den Europeiska åklagarmyndigheten och de utreder anklagelser om att den tidigare partigruppen ID förskingrat 4,3 miljoner euro, motsvarande mer än 47 miljoner kronor, i EU-bidrag. De misstänks ha slussat pengar till lokala partiavdelningar och tilldelat upphandlingar till partivänliga företag, enligt Politico . ” Medan Frankrikes gator håller på att urarta i kaos, verkar myndigheternas prioritet vara detta. Ingen bör låta sig luras av sådana trakasserier ”, skriver Jean-Paul Garraud, ledare för Nationell samling i EU-parlamentet, på X. Oegentligheterna uppdagades när partigruppen ID avvecklades 2024 och till delar blev Patriot. Det kontor som genomsöktes på onsdagsmorgonen tillhör Philip Claeys, tidigare generalsekreterare för ID, som nu innehar samma post hos Patriots. Enligt en tjänsteman förhördes han av EPPO, rapporterar Rapporteur. Genomsökningar genomfördes även i parlamentet i Bryssel. EU-parlamentet har tidigare utrett misstänkt fusk med EU-bidrag, kopplat till gruppen Patriots. 2025 beordrade parlamentets finansdepartement att de skulle betala tillbaka 276 000 euro, som de menar att partigruppen missbrukat i samband med liknande anklagelser. Då anklagade Patriots parlamentet för att bedriva en ”grundlös häxjakt” och menade att gruppen inte gjort något fel. Detta är en nyhetsartikel. articles.summary: SD-toppen Gustav Gellerbrant anmäler Socialdemokraterna för grovt förtal för partiets inlägg i sociala medier om hans påstådda kopplingar till rysk underrättelsesfären genom sin sambo. S säger att man utgått från uppgifter i media.
articles.body_text: SD-toppen Gustav Gellerbrant anmäler Socialdemokraterna för grovt förtal för partiets inlägg i sociala medier om hans påstådda kopplingar till rysk underrättelsesfären genom sin sambo. S säger att man utgått från uppgifter i media. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Strax före valet avslöjade tidningen Expo att SD-toppen Gustav Gellerbrants sambo, som är tjänsteman för Sverigedemokraterna i riksdagen, under flera år hade spridit proryska budskap i sociala medier. Efter avslöjandet gick Gellerbrant på föräldraledighet och har kallat medierapporteringen för ”en omänsklig påfrestning för min familj”. Socialdemokraterna delade ett inlägg i sociala medier om händelsen, där partiet gjorde ett fiktivt CV över Gustav Gellerbrant, där det till exempel står ”2026 - avslöjades ha koppling till ryska underrättelsesfären genom sin sambo, också politisk sekreterare för SD i riksdagen”. Det är det inlägget som Gellerbrant nu polisanmält. – Vi menar på att det Socialdemokratiska Arbetarpartiet har, genom publiceringen av de här anklagelserna mot Gustav, begått ett förtalsbrott, säger Iman Bayazi, juridiskt ombud. – Inlägget kan, i princip, likställas med ett icke-sant brottsregister. Och det gjorde de bara några dagar innan valet 2026. – Inlägget fick ju en sån enorm spridning och delades av andra och så vidare. Så att det är ungefär där domstolarna brukar titta på om det var förtal eller grovt förtal, så att säga. Det är ju faktiskt några av de absolut viktigaste omständigheterna, hur stor spridning detta fick. – Och Socialdemokraterna med sina 80 000 plus-medlemmar och 10 000-tals medlemmar på Facebook , de har ju en enorm makt att sprida saker och ting. Så det är det vi menar gränsar till grovt förtal. Socialdemokraternas presstjänst skriver i en kommentar till Expressen att partiet inväntar stämningsansökan och ska analysera den.

articles.title: Trump: ”Skedde av respekt för Trump”
articles.summary: Amerikanska medborgaren Stephen Hubbard släpptes av Ryssland ”av respekt för Trump”, skriver Trump. Samtidigt säger presidenten att det berodde på lättade sanktioner.
articles.body_text: Amerikanen Stephen Hubbard släpptes av Ryssland utan amerikanska eftergifter. Samtidigt pekar presidenten ut en annan anledning till frigivningen. ”Om sanktioner hade införts skulle dessa förhandlingar med säkerhet ha avbrutits helt och hållet”, skriver han. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Den 74-årige amerikanen Stephen Hubbard greps av ryska styrkor i ockuperade delar av Ukraina 2022. Han anklagades av Kreml för att ha stridit för Ukraina – åtalspunkter som USA :s utrikesdepartement ansåg var falska. Trump säger att Ryssland släppte amerikanen Stephen Hubbard ”av respekt för Trump” – utan fångutbyte. Samtidigt medger han att lättade sanktioner spelade roll. De dubbla beskeden väcker frågor om spelet mellan USA, Ryssland och Ukraina. Under onsdagen släpptes Hubbard plötsligt. Det skedde samtidigt som USA:s särskilda sändebud Steve Witkoff var i Ryssland för att förhandla om nya samtal med Ukraina. Witkoff beskrev Vladimir Putin som ”en människovän” för hans beslut att släppa Hubbard, skriver CNN. Men spelet bakom frisläppningen framstår oklart från president Donald Trumps egna inlägg i sociala medier. Trump skriver att Ryssland släppt Hubbard efter ett telefonsamtal med Putin förra veckan, där Trump uttryckligen bad om att Hubbard skulle få komma hem.
